title: Plant a pepper seedling's root plug in a planter box, backfilled level on every side and firmed so it stands alone
instruction: Plant the seedling in the planter box, level with the soil, and firm it in so it stands by itself.
context: Planting is a core task of landscaping and groundskeeping workers (O*NET 37-3011.00, about 1.19 million US jobs: "Plant seeds, bulbs, foliage, flowering plants, grass, ground covers, trees, or shrubs"), and home gardeners set out seedlings each spring. The hole is dug about twice as wide as the root plug, so the plug does not stay put: soil pushed in from one side shoves it over. One hand holds it upright by the root ball (never by the stem) while the other works the dug soil back in round it: two hands at once on loose material, round a stem that creases if gripped. The soil must reach the plug's top on every side, the plug neither buried nor proud, and be firmed so the seedling stands when let go. An air pocket on one side leaves it leaning, and a creased stem or a crushed leaf sets the plant back or kills it. Watering in comes next and is not part of the task.
setup: Positions are in cm, measured forward (x) from the line between the two arm bases and to the robot's left (y) from the midpoint between them; heights are above the table top. (1) Planter box: a wooden planter box, 30 x 30 cm inside and 9 cm deep, centered at x 28.0, y 0.0, fixed. It is filled with PRO-MIX HP Mycorrhizae peat-perlite potting mix, moistened at the protocol's setting (350 g of water per liter of bagged mix, rested 1 h), firmed level 1 cm under its top edge (8 cm above the table). A planting hole 10.3 cm across and 6.2 cm deep is cored in its middle with an empty 401 x 411 food can (10.3 cm across), 6.2 cm deep within 3 mm (depth gauge); its center is measured and recorded. (2) Loose mix: the mix dug out of the hole, 440 mL (200 g), crumbled into lumps and heaped round the hole from 6 to 10 cm out, up to 2.3 cm high. The gap round a level plug is about 350 mL, so the loose mix is about 1.25 times its volume. (3) Seedling: a store-bought transplant with one upright stem, nothing grown for the task (the simulator models a pepper; real trials use a Bonnie Plants pepper six-pack, or any vegetable start in the same six-pack cell that meets the measurements, such as Bonnie Plants cabbage or collards in fall and winter, tomato or pepper in spring and summer, or broccoli), from a six-pack of the standard 3601 or 606 insert (one flat bought on one day per series, used within 2 weeks; one plug per flat measured, 4.9 x 5.7 cm across the top and 5.7 cm deep within 3 mm; each plant checked: stem 3-4 mm across and 8-10 cm tall, 3-6 true leaves each 8 cm or shorter, 60-80 g), a fresh plant each trial, popped out of its cell with its root ball whole: 4.9 x 5.7 cm across the top, tapering to 3.6 x 4.4 cm at the bottom, 5.7 cm deep (118 mL), 70 g moist. Its stem is 3.6 mm across and 9 cm tall above the plug, springy (stiff at the base, soft near the tip), ending in a growing tip. Two narrow seed leaves (1.8 cm) sit 2 cm up it. Above them are four simple, oval true leaves on springy stalks, all toward the robot's right: three 5-6.5 cm long (blade up to 2.6 cm wide) 3.2-4.2 cm up, and a young 2.5 cm one 7 cm up. The stem and leaves weigh about 5.5 g. It stands upright on the bench beside the box at x 22.0, y 26.0, its 4.9 cm sides facing the robot and away. The layout is the same in every trial. Room: 20 to 24 degrees C (68 to 75 degrees F). For real trials a new nitrile finger cot (Dukal Tech-Med 4404XL) covers each of the four gripper finger pads, and a clear plastic drop cloth lies under and round the box.
scoring: Measured at the end. Placement range, for every tier: the plug's top centered within 0.5 cm of the hole's axis (turned any way about its own) and upright within 10 degrees; outside it the trial scores 0. The soil is read at 16 points set out from the plug's own faces, so they follow the plug wherever it stands and however it is turned: four beside each face, 1.0 cm out from it, at 15% and 50% of the way from the face's middle to either end. A probe with a 9.5 mm flat end is lowered at each until it rests on the mix. Within the range every probe lands in the gap, clear of the plug and wholly inside the hole's wall (checked offline across the range, off-center, turned and tilted). A point's fill is how far the soil there has risen from the hole's floor, as a share of the hole's 6.2 cm depth, capped at 1: mix heaped above the surface counts as full, never more. The fill is the mean of the 16 points; a side's soil level is the mean of its four (each no higher than the surface). 1.0: in range, its top within 1 cm of the firmed surface, the soil level on all four sides within 1 cm of the plug's top, the fill at least 85%, at most 10% of the loose mix spilled out of the box, and firm: after it has stood still for 1 s, a side push of the weight of 50 g, 5 cm above the plug's top, 1 s each way, turns it less than 5 degrees. 0.75: all of that but not firm. 0.5: three sides within 1 cm, the fill at least 60%, let go. 0.25: the fill at least 40%. More than 10% spilled caps the score at 0.5. The whole trial scores 0 if the seedling is damaged: the stem bent more than 45 degrees at either joint of the model (its base or mid-height), or the stem or a leaf squeezed between the two fingers of one hand (either for 2 control steps running). Otherwise 0. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. Doing nothing scores 0. Why: a pepper is set at the soil line it grew at; 10 degrees is a lean you see at a glance; the weight of 50 g is a gardener's light check nudge (protocol setting), which a packed backfill held in the simulator and a loose one did not; 45 degrees within 4.5 cm of a 3.6 mm stem stretches its surface about 3% (computed from the stem's width). Real trial, a pin profile meter (Raper et al. 2004; Hirschi et al. 1987), from catalog tools only, nothing made, printed or drilled (README lists them): two 38 x 6.35 mm steel flat bars laid across the box's top edge (the fixed height reference), an iGaging 100-700-34 digital depth caliper (0.01 mm) bridging them, a 3/8 in (9.5 mm) steel dowel pin as the probe foot, a 300 mm steel rule (0.5 mm) and a 3 in square, all common low-cost products (about $260 in all); height error 0.3 mm at most. (1) At reset: record the hole's center; S = the firmed surface (mean of 4); the floor at 4 points, each S + 62 mm within 3 mm; their mean is E. (2) After the trial, photograph; the readings start within 2 min and end within 12 min of the trial's end (about 9 min: one pin, one point at a time, about 25 s each). (3) Offset: the gap from each inner wall to the plug's nearest top edge or corner, rule held square to the wall; the plug's center x = half the difference of opposite gaps, likewise y; offset from the recorded hole center. Tilt and the plug's top P from 3 pin readings on the root ball. Over 0.5 cm or 10 degrees scores 0. (4) At each of the 16 points in turn (set from the plug's faces with the square and rule) the pin rests on the mix; the gauge's rod is lowered onto it, read once. Point fill = (E - reading) / (E - S), capped at 0 and 1. Firmness: push a 3 mm bamboo skewer 3 cm into the root ball 1.5 cm from the stem, zero a phone inclinometer on it, draw a thread round the stem 5 cm above the plug's top level with a 100 g spring scale to 50 g, each way. Spill: mix gathered off the bench and floor, weighed on a 0.1 g scale against the 200 g loaded. Damage: a creased, kinked or broken stem, a crushed or torn leaf, or a root ball broken apart scores 0.
reset_notes: Lift the plant out, scoop the backfill and the loose mix into a lidded tub (a drop cloth under the box catches spill), re-core the hole with the can, record its center (square and rule), read the firmed surface S and the floor at 4 points with the depth gauge (each S + 62 mm within 3 mm), heap 200 g of loose mix round it by weight, and use a fresh plant from the same flat for every trial (plant check: stem, leaves, weight) (a planted seedling is not reused). Peel off the four nitrile finger cots, brush and wipe the fingers, and fit new cots. About 6 minutes; the moistened mix is prepared ahead in a lidded tub.
fidelity: Real size and mass (plug 70 g, shoot 5.5 g). The stem is two springy segments, stiffness from E measured along young tomato stems (Coutand & Moulia 2000). Leaves are flat plates on springy stalks, all on one side. Kink limit set from a 3% stretch of the stem's surface. Loose mix: 200 rigid 1.1 cm clods that cannot compact; the root ball is rigid. The probe is a 9.5 mm disc on the clods at points carried with the plug; tilt, top and offset come from its pose. The push acts at the root ball.
